title: William Gunston's 'Tower of London' remark on charged wing edges

tellings.quote: because I don't want to end up in the Tower of London.

plain: The writer William Gunston, in a history of aircraft engine technology printed in the aviation magazine Air International, is said to have touched on the idea of electrically charging the edges of aircraft wings and then stopped short, saying he would go no further "because I don't want to end up in the Tower of London," the old London fortress once used as a royal prison. Michels brings up the remark himself, crediting that magazine piece. He raises it because, if meant seriously, it would hint that the subject was a guarded state secret in Britain.
